mainTopic: Defining the מלאכות in the משנה's list, from טוחן through קורע, and finding their sources in the משכן
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of sorting lupines: because they rot if left in place, taking them out counts as removing פסולת from אוכל. The גמרא then goes through the משנה's list of מלאכות. Chopping beets or wood chips finely is טוחן, and cutting to an exact size is also מחתך. The משנה lists אופה instead of cooking dyes because it follows the order of making bread. Heating a wooden peg in an oven and boiling pitch both count as מבשל, even though each item ends up hard. רבא and אביי count how many separate חטאות come from making a clay barrel, an oven, or a reed basket. רבי יוחנן and רב כהנא argue about spinning wool while it is still on an animal, and ריש לקיש explains the three מלאכות involved in working on a feather. The גמרא searches for the משכן source of קושר and מתיר and settles on the חלזון trappers' nets. It explains that sewing two stitches counts only when the thread is tied. Finally, it asks where there was tearing in the משכן, and the answer by רבה and רבי זירא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why sorting lupines counts as removing waste from food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the lupine case. Lupines are boiled many times, and if the food is not taken out it rots, so taking it out is treated like removing waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they boil it seven times, and if they do not take it out, it rots. So it is treated like taking waste out of food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous section about sorting lupines on שבת. It explains why taking out the edible part is treated as removing waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, taking food out of waste is the allowed way to sort. Here, though, the lupine food rots and spoils everything if it is left in place, so it acts like the 'bad' part. That turns the act into removing פסולת from אוכל, which is the forbidden kind of בורר.

keyTerms.meaning: removing waste from food (the forbidden form of sorting)
it is like, it is treated as

steps.whatToRemember: Whether something counts as 'waste' depends on how it acts in practice, not only on what it looks like. Lupines that rot if left in place are treated like waste being removed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying lupines are not food. They are food. The point is that in this situation, taking them out works like removing פסולת, so the law of בורר treats it as an exception.

phrases.english: for they boil it seven times,
and if they do not take it out, it rots —
so it is like removing waste from food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the lupine discussion that began on the previous amud
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: the food functions as waste
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Taking lupines out should be ordinary, permitted sorting of food from waste
steps.terutzMaskana: Because lupines rot if left in place, taking them out counts as removing פסולת from אוכל

steps.title: Chopping beets finely counts as grinding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'one who grinds' from the משנה. רב פפא rules that chopping beets into small pieces makes a person liable for טוחן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה lists 'one who grinds.' רב פפא said: someone who chops beets into small pieces is liable for grinding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next מלאכה in the משנה, grinding. רב פפא gives an example of grinding that does not involve a mill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grinding is basically breaking something into tiny pieces. Chopping a vegetable very finely does the same thing, so it falls under טוחן even without a grinder.

phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה's list of מלאכות

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the מלאכה of טוחן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Chopping beets finely is a form of טוחן

steps.title: Chopping wood chips counts as grinding
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה gives a second example: chopping wood into small chips is also טוחן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשה said: someone who chops wood into chips is liable for grinding.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא adds another example of grinding, this time with something that is not food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that טוחן is not only about food. Breaking any material, even wood, into small bits fits the category.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case to רב פפא's ruling

steps.title: Cutting to an exact size adds liability for cutting
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds that if the person cuts carefully to a specific size, he is also liable for מחתך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: if he is careful about the measurement, he is liable for cutting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a further point to the wood-chip case. If the chips are cut to an exact size, there is also the separate מלאכה of cutting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grinding is just making small pieces. מחתך is cutting something to a specific, intended size. When a person cares about the measurement, his act matches מחתך as well.

keyTerms.meaning: cutting to size, one of the 39 מלאכות

steps.whatToRemember: Chopping things into small bits is טוחן. Cutting them to an exact size is also מחתך.

phrases.english: if he is particular about the measurement —
he is liable because of cutting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִי קָפֵיד אַמִּשְׁחֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second category of liability to the case in step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting with care for exact size is מחתך

steps.title: Why does the משנה list baking instead of cooking dyes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'kneading and baking.' רב פפא asks why the משנה left out cooking dye-spices, which was done in the משכן, and listed baking, which was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה lists 'one who kneads and one who bakes.' רב פפא said: our תנא left out cooking spices, which was done in the משכן, and listed baking instead?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the next items in the משנה, kneading and baking. רב פפא raises a difficulty about why baking is on the list at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מלאכות are learned from the work done to build the משכן. Dyes were cooked there, but bread was not baked for the building. So it seems the משנה should have listed בישול סממנין rather than אופה.

keyTerms.meaning: our תנא, the author of our משנה
cooking spices or herbs to make dyes
the Tabernacle, the source of the 39 מלאכות

phrases.english: And one who kneads and one who bakes.
cooking spices, which was done in the Tabernacle,

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבַק תַּנָּא דִידַן בִּישּׁוּל סַמְמָנִין דַּהֲוָה בְּמִשְׁכָּן וּנְקַט אוֹפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the wording of the משנה's list
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice to list אופה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מלאכות come from the משכן. Cooking dyes was done there and baking was not, so the list seems to have the wrong item.

steps.title: The משנה follows the order of making bread
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the תנא organized the list around the steps of making bread, so he wrote 'baking.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Our תנא followed the order of making bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered. The משנה lists the מלאכות in the order of making bread, from plowing through baking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baking and cooking are the same מלאכה of applying heat. The תנא chose the name 'baking' because it fits the bread sequence, not because cooking is excluded.
steps.whatToRemember: אופה in the משנה stands for the cooking category in general. It was chosen to complete the bread sequence.
steps.confusionAlert: Cooking is not missing from the 39 מלאכות. It is included under the name אופה.

phrases.english: Our Tanna followed the order of bread-making.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the organizing principle of the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה wrongly left out the cooking done in the משכן
steps.terutzMaskana: The list follows the bread sequence, and אופה covers cooking

steps.title: Putting a wooden peg into an oven counts as cooking
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב עוירא rules that putting a wooden peg into an oven makes a person liable for מבשל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב עוירא said: someone who puts a peg into an oven is liable for cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling about the מלאכה of cooking. Heating a wooden peg in an oven counts as cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking is not only for food. Using heat to change the state of any material, even wood, fits מבשל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב עַוִּירָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Avira said:
one who puts a peg into an oven —

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב עַוִּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the cooking category connected to אופה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heating a wooden peg in an oven is מבשל

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this ruling needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling as too obvious to need stating. This sets up an explanation of the new point it teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting something into fire and changing it is plainly a heat-based act. The challenge pushes the גמרא to find the real חידוש.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 7 adds anything new
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר רב עוירא's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Heating a peg is clearly cooking, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The wood softens first, then hardens
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think the goal is to harden the tool, which is the opposite of cooking. The ruling teaches that the wood first softens and only then hardens.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said he only intends to strengthen the tool. So he teaches us that it first softens and then hardens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point. Even though the final goal is to harden the peg, the wood softens in the oven first, and that softening is cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking usually softens things, while here the end result is hardening. One might think this is not cooking at all. The ruling teaches that the softening stage along the way is real cooking.

phrases.english: that he intends to strengthen the utensil,
that it first softens and then hardens.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא לְשָׁרוֹרֵי מָנָא קָא מִיכַּוֵין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hardening a tool is the opposite of cooking, so it is not מבשל
steps.terutzMaskana: The wood softens first, and that softening counts as cooking

steps.title: Boiling pitch counts as cooking
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that boiling pitch makes a person liable for מבשל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: someone who boils pitch is liable for cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ruling about cooking a non-food material: melting pitch by boiling it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pitch is hard, melts when heated, and hardens again as it cools. The ruling counts the melting as cooking.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to the peg ruling

steps.title: Isn't this also obvious?
steps.stepSummary: Again the גמרא asks why this ruling needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again challenges the ruling as obvious. This sets up the explanation of what it teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boiling is the most basic form of cooking. The question forces the גמרא to show the real new point.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10, the same pattern as step 8

steps.title: A temporary change still counts as cooking
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think that because the pitch hardens again, the boiling does not count. The ruling teaches that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since it goes back and hardens again, say it is not cooking. So he teaches us that it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point. Even though the pitch returns to being hard, the melting still counts as cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pitch starts hard and ends hard, so it might seem that nothing lasting was done. The ruling teaches that a temporary change caused by heat is still מבשל.
steps.whatToRemember: Cooking means a real change caused by heat, even in non-food items like wood or pitch, and even if the item later returns to its earlier state.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together, the peg and pitch cases show that מבשל is defined by heat changing a material, not by what the final product looks like.

phrases.english: since it goes back and hardens,
so he teaches us that it does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge in step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the pitch hardens again, the boiling is not considered cooking
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a temporary change from heat is מבשל

steps.title: Making a barrel or an oven brings many sin-offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that making a clay barrel on שבת involves seven מלאכות, and making an oven involves eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Someone who makes a clay barrel is liable for seven sin-offerings. Someone who makes an oven is liable for eight.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא teaches that making one clay object on שבת can involve many separate forbidden labors. Each labor brings its own חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a barrel takes seven steps, and each one is a separate אב מלאכה: grinding the dirt, sorting out stones, kneading, cutting the clay, building, lighting the fire, and baking. An oven adds one more step, smoothing the final layer, so it comes to eight. The point is that one finished product can be made of many separate חיובים.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offerings, brought for doing a forbidden act on שבת by mistake

phrases.english: One who makes a clay barrel
An oven: he is liable for eight sin-offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דַּעֲבַד חָבִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new theme: how many separate מלאכות are done in making one object.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A barrel is seven חטאות and an oven is eight.

steps.title: Making a reed basket brings eleven or thirteen sin-offerings
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that making a reed basket involves eleven מלאכות, and thirteen if he also sews its opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Someone who makes a reed basket is liable for eleven sin-offerings. If he also sews its opening, he is liable for thirteen.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a similar count for making a reed basket. Sewing the opening adds two more labors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the basket includes cutting and preparing the reeds, which covers reaping, planting, gathering, sorting, smoothing, grinding, and measured cutting. It also includes the weaving steps and building. Sewing the mouth adds sewing and tying, which brings the total to thirteen.

phrases.english: One who makes a reed basket
And if he sewed its opening,
he is liable for thirteen sin-offerings.
phrases.notes: The added two are sewing and tying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַאן דַּעֲבַד חַלְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel count for a different object.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A reed basket is eleven חטאות, and thirteen if the opening is sewn.
steps.whatToRemember: One finished object can involve many separate מלאכות, and each one brings its own חטאת.

steps.title: Spinning wool while it is still on the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about shearing and whitening wool. Then רבי יוחנן rules that spinning wool on a live animal brings three חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה listed shearing wool and whitening it. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Someone who spins wool that is still on an animal on שבת is liable for three sin-offerings: one for shearing, one for combing, and one for spinning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the list of מלאכות in the משנה and reaches shearing and whitening wool. It then brings רבי יוחנן's case of spinning wool while it is still attached to the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spinning wool on the animal pulls the wool off, which counts as גוזז. It also loosens and separates the fibers, which counts as מנפץ, and it twists them into thread, which counts as טווה. So one act covers three מלאכות.

phrases.english: One who shears the wool and one who whitens it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הַטּוֹוֶה צֶמֶר שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה בְּשַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: One who spins wool that is on an animal's back on Shabbat

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next items in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spinning wool on a live animal brings three חטאות: גוזז, מנפץ, and טווה.

steps.title: רב כהנא: this is not the normal way to do these labors
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא disagrees. He holds that shearing, combing, and spinning are not normally done this way, so there is no חיוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: This is not the normal way of shearing, it is not the normal way of combing, and it is not the normal way of spinning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא argues on רבי יוחנן. Nobody normally does these labors while the wool is still on the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a person is only liable when he does a מלאכה in its usual way. Since nobody spins wool on a live animal, רב כהנא holds there is no liability for any of the three labors.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not the usual way

phrases.english: This is not the usual way of shearing,
and this is not the usual way of combing,
and this is not the usual way of spinning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: אֵין דֶּרֶךְ גְּזִיזָה בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An opposing view to רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unusual way of doing a מלאכה is not liable.

steps.title: Challenge: in the משכן they spun hair right on the goats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא from a ברייתא of רבי נחמיה, which says the women spun goat hair while it was still on the goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really not the normal way? But a ברייתא taught in the name of רבי נחמיה: They washed the hair on the goats and spun it on the goats. So spinning on an animal does count as spinning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב כהנא's claim that spinning on an animal is not normal. It brings a source showing that this was done in the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מלאכות of שבת are learned from the work of the משכן. If the women spun goat hair while it was on the goats, then this method was used there. That suggests it is a real way of spinning.

phrases.english: But it was taught in the name of Rabbi Neḥemya:
washed on the goats, and spun on the goats,
This shows that spinning on an animal's back

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב כהנא's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that spinning on an animal is not the normal way
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It was done in the משכן, which is the model for all the מלאכות.

steps.title: Extraordinary skill is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that what was done in the משכן required unusual wisdom, so it does not show what is normal for ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Extraordinary wisdom is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב כהנא. The women in the משכן had special skill, and ordinary people cannot spin this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What a few gifted people can do does not set the normal way of doing a מלאכה. Because spinning on the animal needs special skill, for everyone else it is still an unusual method, and they are not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra or extraordinary wisdom and skill

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say that the women in the משכן did not really spin. It says their method was special, so it does not define the normal way for everyone else.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: unusual skill versus normal practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משכן proves that spinning on an animal is the normal way.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a special skill, so for ordinary people it is still not the normal way.

steps.title: Working on a feather brings three sin-offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that plucking a feather, snipping its tip, and stripping its fibers bring three חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Someone who plucks a feather from a wing, snips it, and strips it is liable for three sin-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about working on a bird's feather. It lists three acts that make a person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us there are three separate חיובים here. It does not yet say which מלאכה each act falls under. The next step explains that.

keyTerms.meaning: A wing, here meaning a wing feather

phrases.english: One who plucks the wing feather
and snips it and strips it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case of one process that holds several מלאכות, connected to shearing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plucking, snipping, and stripping a feather bring three חטאות.

steps.title: ריש לקיש explains the three labors
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that plucking is גוזז, snipping is מחתך, and stripping is ממחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: Plucking is liable as shearing, snipping is liable as cutting, and stripping is liable as smoothing.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש tells us which אב מלאכה each of the three feather acts falls under.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling a feather off a bird is like removing wool from a sheep, so it is גוזז. Cutting the tip to a set size is מחתך. Stripping the fibers leaves a smooth quill, so it is ממחק.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
One who plucks is liable for shearing,
one who snips is liable for cutting,
one who strips is liable for smoothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תולש is גוזז, קוטם is מחתך, and ממרט is ממחק.

steps.title: Where was there tying in the משכן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's listing of tying and untying and asks where tying took place in the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה listed tying and untying. Where was there tying in the משכן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches קושר and מתיר in the משנה. Since every מלאכה must come from the משכן, it asks where tying was done there. This question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אב מלאכה needs a source in the work of the משכן. The גמרא wants to find a real, lasting tying that was done there.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tabernacle, which is the source of the מלאכות of שבת

phrases.english: One who ties and one who unties.
Where was there tying in the Tabernacle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next pair in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source in the משכן for the מלאכה of tying

steps.title: רבא: they tied the tents to pegs
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that they tied the tent coverings of the משכן to pegs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They tied the tents to pegs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a first answer: the coverings of the משכן were tied to pegs in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These ropes were knots used in the משכן, so they seem like a good source for קושר. The next step will question whether this kind of knot is the right kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Tents, here meaning the coverings of the משכן

phrases.english: For they tied the tents to pegs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tying the tent ropes to pegs

steps.title: Rejected: those knots were meant to be untied
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's answer, because the tent knots were temporary and made in order to be untied.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that tying? That was tying in order to untie!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's answer. The tent knots were not lasting knots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Jews traveled, they took the משכן apart and untied all those knots. A temporary knot does not make one liable on שבת, so it cannot be the source for the מלאכה of קושר.

keyTerms.meaning: In order to untie, meaning a temporary knot

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא קוֹשֵׁר עַל מְנָת לְהַתִּיר הוּא.
phrases.english: That is tying in order to untie.

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹשְׁרִים?! הָהוּא קוֹשֵׁר עַל מְנָת לְהַתִּיר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The tent-peg source as a whole
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It was a temporary knot, and a temporary knot is not liable.

steps.title: אביי: weavers tied torn threads
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the weavers of the משכן's curtains tied a thread back together when it broke.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: The curtain weavers, when a thread tore, would tie it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a new source for tying. When a thread broke during weaving, the weavers tied it together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This knot stayed inside the curtain, so it was a lasting knot. That solves the problem raised against רבא's answer.

phrases.english: when a thread tore for them,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שֶׁכֵּן אוֹרְגֵי יְרִיעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tying torn threads in the curtains, which is a lasting knot

steps.title: רבא: what about untying?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי: his answer explains tying, but where was untying done in the משכן?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You explained tying. What can be said about untying?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points out that אביי's answer only covers half of the pair. The משנה lists untying too, and it also needs a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A good source should explain both קושר and מתיר. אביי's weaver case gives tying but no untying, so the source is incomplete.

phrases.english: untying, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּרֵצְתְּ קוֹשֵׁר, מַתִּיר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It gives no source for מתיר.

steps.title: A suggested answer: untying one of two nearby knots
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests a possible answer for אביי: if two knots ended up next to each other, the weaver untied one and tied one again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: if two knots happened to be next to each other, he would untie one and tie one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a possible answer on אביי's behalf so that he can reject it. This step sets up the rejection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that two knots close together looked bad. The weaver would undo one knot and keep the other, and that would be a case of untying.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer)

phrases.english: that if it happened to him
two knots next to each other,
he unties one and leaves one tied —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible defense of אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A suggested answer that will be rejected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no untying in the weaving at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The suggestion is that untying happened when two knots ended up next to each other. Step 27 rejects this.

steps.title: Rejected: a knotted curtain is not fit for ה'
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the suggestion. Even for a human king, people would not make a curtain full of knots, so certainly not for הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, before a king of flesh and blood people do not do this. Before the King of kings, הקדוש ברוך הוא, would they do it?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the suggested answer with a קל וחומר. A curtain with knots in it would never be used in the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a human king would not accept a knotted curtain, then certainly the משכן would not have one. The weavers would replace the thread rather than leave knots. So the weaving gives no source for untying, and אביי's answer falls.

keyTerms.meaning: A king of flesh and blood, meaning a human king
The King of kings, meaning ה'

phrases.english: Now, before a king of flesh and blood
the Holy One, Blessed be He, would one do so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם אֵין עוֹשִׂין כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The two-knots answer, and with it אביי's source for the pair
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A knotted curtain would never be used in the משכן.

steps.title: Final answer: the חלזון trappers tied and untied
steps.stepSummary: רבא, or some say רבי עילאי, answers that the trappers of the חלזון tied and untied their nets.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, and some say רבי עילאי said: The trappers of the חלזון would tie and untie.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final source for the pair. The people who caught the חלזון, used for the blue dye of the משכן, tied and untied knots in their nets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fishermen tie their nets and also untie them to make changes. This gives a source in the work of the משכן for both קושר and מתיר together, which solves רבא's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The sea creature used to make the blue dye (תכלת)

steps.whatToRemember: The משכן source for קושר and מתיר is the חלזון trappers' nets. Tent pegs fail because those knots were temporary. Curtain weavers fail because their work gives no source for untying.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that each מלאכה needs a real and lasting source in the משכן, and that a pair like קושר and מתיר needs a source for both parts.

phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Elai said:
For the trappers of the ḥilazon

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי עִילַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new source after the earlier ones were rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חלזון trappers tied and untied their nets.

steps.title: Two stitches do not last
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about sewing two stitches and asks how this can count, since two stitches do not stay in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one who sews two stitches.' But two stitches do not last!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item from the משנה, sewing two stitches. Then it immediately challenges it: two stitches will just slip out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, an act that does not last is usually not a full מלאכה. Two loose stitches pull out right away. So how can the משנה make someone liable for sewing only two?
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether sewing is a מלאכה. Sewing clearly is one. The question is only whether such a small, weak amount of sewing is enough to make someone liable.

phrases.english: And one who sews two stitches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from קושר and מתיר to the next מלאכה in the משנה, sewing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that sewing two stitches makes a person liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מלאכה whose result does not last is not a real מלאכה, and two stitches do not last.

steps.title: Only when he tied the ends
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the משנה means a case where the sewer tied knots at the ends of the thread, so the stitches stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן said: It counts only when he tied them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. The משנה is talking about someone who tied the thread after sewing the two stitches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ends are knotted, the two stitches can no longer slip out. Now the sewing lasts, so it is a full מלאכה. The answer limits the משנה to a specific case. It does not deny that sewing two stitches can count.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports רבי יוחנן's teaching

steps.whatToRemember: Two stitches count as sewing only when the thread is tied, because then the stitches last.

phrases.english: That is, where he tied them.
phrases.notes: He knotted the thread so that the stitches hold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְהוּא שֶׁקְּשָׁרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case (אוקימתא) to a sewer who tied the thread.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two plain stitches unravel, so they should not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is speaking of tied stitches, which last, so the person is liable.

steps.title: Was there tearing in the משכן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's item 'one who tears in order to sew' and asks where tearing ever happened in the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who tears in order to sew.' Was there tearing in the משכן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next מלאכה, tearing in order to sew. It asks what tearing in the משכן this מלאכה is based on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every main מלאכה must come from work that was done for the משכן. It is not obvious that anyone ever tore anything while building the משכן. So the גמרא wants to know where this מלאכה came from.

phrases.english: One who tears in order to sew.
Was there tearing in the Mishkan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern as the earlier question about tying in step 21: where was this done in the משכן?
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of tearing as a main מלאכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A main מלאכה needs a source in the משכן, and tearing does not seem to have one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source in the משכן for the מלאכה of tearing in order to sew

steps.title: רבה and רבי זירא begin their answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces an answer that both רבה and רבי זירא said. The answer itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רבי זירא both said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the answer to 'Was there tearing in the משכן?' The actual explanation comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two אמוראים are giving the same answer. Here we only get the names. The content of the answer is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who says this answer together with רבה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for the answer in this line. The source text stops here, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

phrases.notes: Introduces their answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 31's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the names of the people answering appear here. The answer itself is on the next amud.
